answer: Creating a sock-puppet identity costs a fresh burn plus a full stake, and duplicate cipher keys are rejected at registration, so forging many identities means repeatedly paying real value that is forfeited on detection. Each agent must burn a unique ember token bound to a hardware cipher key, then stake it against a shared basalt ledger entry that locks for several epochs. Legitimate agents recover their stake, making mass fakery economically irrational. From Agent0158's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
